label: DEEP-RESEARCH TASK: study OPTISIGNS' app library specifically. Use WebSearch + WebFetch o

findings.summary:
OptiSigns ships a marketplace of 140–160+ "Apps" surfaced at optisigns.com/apps (and /apps-list-category), organized into ~8 category tabs (Misc, News, Finance, Social Media, Photos & Video, File Management, Communication, Business) plus an "All" view, with a search box, ~10 pages of paginated app cards, and a per-card PLAN BADGE ("Included in all plans" / "Standard plan and up" / "Pro Plus plan and up"). The flow is: in the dashboard you go to Files/Assets → "App" → pick a named app → fill a polished per-app config form → it SAVES AS AN ASSET that you then drop into playlists/schedules and assign to screens — i.e. an "App" output is a reusable content asset, distinct from "Designer" (their Canva-style template editor) and from raw "Website"/"Embed" URL apps. Most marketed apps are social (Instagram, Facebook, X, TikTok via "Social Media Walls", Google Reviews, Yelp, LinkedIn), data/dashboards (Power BI, Tableau, Looker Studio, Google Sheets, Salesforce, Zendesk, HubSpot, Smartsheet, Airtable), Google/Microsoft Workspace (Slides, Calendar, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams, Slack), and free first-party feeds (Weather, free Sports feeds for NFL/NBA/NHL/MLB/NCAA/F1/soccer, News). HONEST 2026 embed reality: social walls require Meta OAuth (Business accounts only) or OptiSigns' own aggregator backend; Power BI rides a public "synced" embed URL on free tiers and a secured-login dashboard on Pro Plus; "secured" dashboards + dynamic data (birthdays, queues) need their Pro-Plus OptiSync data-mapping. Free plan caps you at 25 basic apps (locked apps shown with a red lock); 100+ apps unlock on Standard, dynamic data + secured dashboards on Pro Plus. Almost every one of these maps onto a VenueOS widget we already ship (WEBPAGE, SOCIAL_FEED, RSS_FEED, STREAMING, LIVE_DATA, WEATHER, CALENDAR, CHART, IMAGE_CAROUSEL) — the gap is curation/branding/per-app config UX, not core capability.</summary>

<uxNotes>[
"Single entry point: a marketing app gallery at /apps (and /apps-list-category) AND an in-product picker. In-product you add an app from Files/Assets via an 'App' button → choose the named app → fill its config → it SAVES AS A REUSABLE ASSET you then drop into playlists/schedules and assign to screens. The 'asset' abstraction is key: an app instance is a content object, not a one-off zone.",
"Category tabs across the top: All, Misc, News, Finance, Social Media, Photos & Video, File Management, Communication, Business — plus a search box with a clear/close button. ~10 pages of paginated cards (logo + name + plan badge).",
"Every app card carries a PLAN-AVAILABILITY BADGE — 'Included in all plans' / 'Standard plan and up' / 'Pro Plus plan and up' — so gating is visible before you click. Free plan shows locked apps with a RED LOCK icon and blocks asset creation on them (clear upsell, not a dead end).",
"Each app has its own polished marketing detail page (/apps-list/<app>) with a screenshot of the actual config form, a one-line value prop, a 'Learn how it works' link to a step-by-step support article, and the plan badge. The config UI is genuinely per-app (Instagram: view-mode/theme/speed/font-size/moderation/QR; Website: URL + refresh interval), not a generic key-value form.",
"They distinguish 'Apps' (live data/integrations that become assets) from 'Designer' (their Canva-style template/content editor with 1000+ templates) and from raw 'Website'/'Embed' URL apps. Three clearly-separated authoring surfaces.",
"Free first-party feeds (Weather, Sports, News, Crypto, Currency, Stock) are positioned as a big lure: 'free on every plan,' ~2-minute add. The friction-free first-party feeds are what get a new user a live screen fast; the OAuth integrations are the upsell.",
"OptiSync 'Dynamic Data Mapping' (Pro Plus) is a cross-cutting layer: a Google Sheet (or other source) becomes a DataSource that powers birthday lists, queues, rosters, menu prices — one data engine reused across many 'apps.' Smart architecture: the apps are thin templates over a shared data-binding core.",
"'Virtual Screen' app generates a shareable live-preview URL of a screen — used for remote/WFH preview and demos. A neat productized feature most signage tools bury.",
"Slack/Teams apps invert the model: instead of pulling content IN, you push a message to the screen by typing @optisigns in chat — a chat-bot/inbound-webhook pattern that lowers the bar to 'post to the TV.'"
]</uxNotes>
<doBetterIdeas>[
"Concierge-auto-config the app: OptiSigns still makes the operator pick the app AND fill the form. Our Integration-Discovery + AI Concierge already scrape the operator's URL — so we can SKIP the picker: detect 'this venue has Instagram @x, Toast POS, Google Business reviews' and pre-stage the matching app instances with fields filled, one-tap to accept. Beat their browse-then-configure with detect-then-confirm.",
"Be honest about embed reality in the picker UI: each app card should show its real connection method + a confidence/ToS badge ('Meta Business login required', 'public dashboard URL', 'needs paid X API'). OptiSigns hides this until you're deep in a support article; surfacing it up front prevents the #1 frustration (operator picks Instagram, then learns they need a Business account).",
"Lean on what we already own to leapfrog: we ship WEBPAGE/STREAMING/RSS/SOCIAL_FEED/LIVE_DATA/WEATHER/CALENDAR/CHART today. ~70% of OptiSigns' 140 apps are thin config wrappers over capabilities we already have — we can launch a 40-app library in S/M effort by just adding per-app config forms + logos over existing widgets. The differentiator is curation + branding, not new infra.",
"One shared DataSource engine like OptiSync, but exposed to ALL tiers (not just Pro Plus): a Google Sheet / CSV / our own POS feed powers menus, birthdays, rosters, leaderboards, now-serving. We already have the POS + menu-management pipeline (per-location pricing, auto-86) — productize that as the data-mapping layer so dozens of 'apps' are templates over it.",
"Auto-brand every app instance: OptiSigns' app outputs look generic. Pipe our BrandKit (var(--brand-primary)/accent + fonts) into every app's config by default so an operator's Instagram wall / weather / countdown comes out on-brand instantly — Canva-grade look without effort.",
"Chromium-83-safe app cards by design: flag heavy apps (custom JS embeds, some streaming players, backdrop-blur designs) as 'LCD-only' vs 'LED-safe' in the picker, and auto-pick a degraded variant when the target screen is a Taurus LED. OptiSigns has no such awareness; our locked-down-player reality makes this a real trust win.",
"AI 'build me this app': operator types 'show our 5 latest Instagram posts next to today's lunch menu and a QR to our site' → Concierge composes the multi-app zone layout, brand-applied, ready to assign. We already have AI-authored HTML boards; extend it to compose app instances, not just static design.",
"Live preview + 'send to one screen to test' before publish — combine OptiSigns' Virtual-Screen idea with a one-tap 'preview on a real screen' so operators verify an app renders (and survives the iframe sandbox) before fleet-wide assign.",
"De-risk the social apps with a managed aggregator option: instead of forcing each tenant through Meta/X API approval, offer a VenueOS-managed social-feed backend (the way OptiSigns quietly does) so the operator just pastes a handle — with clear ToS/rate-limit guardrails and a graceful 'last known posts' cache for offline LED players."
]</doBetterIdeas>
